newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton seen falling in Pakistan, easing in India.
newsitem.headline: Cotton seen falling in Pakistan, easing in India.

text.p: Cotton rates are likely to fall in Pakistan next week on arrival of the new crop and ease in India before monsoon rains, dealers said on Friday.
The first cotton from the new crop arrived at a ginning factory in central Pakistan overnight and dealers said domestic prices could fall as more cotton flows in.

Nasim Usman, a dealer at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA), said the crop, which had been expected to arrive in early July, had ripened early due to hot weather in the southern province of Sindh.
The first lot of 100 375-lb bales of NIAB-78 reached a ginning factory in Chichavatni in Punjab province, said Usman.
He said some ginning units would start work in Sindh next week. Prices of old-crop cotton might dip 50 rupees ($1.23) per maund (37.32 kg) soon, Usman added.

Pakistan has fixed a production target of 10 million bales for 1997/98, up from 8.78 million produced in 1996/97, which fell short of the government's target of 10 million. This year's crop was affected by bad weather and insect attacks.
The Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association said on Thursday this year's harvest had reached a provisional 8.78 million bales by June 15, down from 9.938 million at the same time a year ago.

KCA's official spot rates for old-crop NIAB-78 fell 11 rupees to 2,229 on Friday, K-68 11 to 2,432.50 and MNH-93 16.50 to 2,431.50 on news of the first arrival of the new crop.

In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was quoted at 2,100/2,225 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), K-68 at 2,400/2,425 and MNH-93 at 2,400/2,425.
The KCA said Pakistan had shipped 102,068 bales by June 14 out of 121,274 booked for export by June 16, compared to 1.821 million and 2.32 million respectively a year earlier.
In India, cotton prices fell back this week. Demand resistance from yarn and textile mills capped a recent rally while arrival of monsoon rains dampened prices, dealers said.

In spot, Gujarat Kalyan fell 300/800 rupees to 14,200/14,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Wagad cotton lost 400/500 rupees to 12,900/13,000 rupees per candy and Kala-ginned slid 400/500 rupees to 12,200/12,300 rupees per candy.
Traders estimated unsold cotton stocks in the western state of Gujarat, a major cotton-producing region, at 700,000/800,000 (170-kg) bales.

"Commencement of monsoon rains has triggered heavy selling by traders and farmers in Gujarat. A setback in the prices of Gujarat cotton also affected market sentiment in Punjab varieties," one broker said.
Punjab saw-ginned lost 25 rupees to 1,825/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Bengal-deshi fell 10/20 rupees to 1,030/1,070 rupees per maund.
Demand from spinners remained low due to sluggish overseas buying for Indian cotton yarn though some state-owned agencies finalised export deals for about 300,000 bales, dealers said.

"Cotton prices are expected to remain subdued in the coming days taking into consideration the anticipated progress of monsoon rains and stocks lying unsold in the Gujarat region," another dealer said.
($1 = 40.49 Pakistani rupees)
